identity.title: Comparative genomics of canine Leptospira interrogans ST17 strains reveals conserved gene content across heterogeneous clinical presentations.

content.abstract: Leptospira interrogans causes infections ranging from asymptomatic renal carriage to fatal acute disease. Whether this phenotypic variation is encoded in genomic content remains unresolved, and autochthonous strains from natural infections are underrepresented in comparative datasets. Eight Leptospira stains from naturally infected dogs in an endemic Brazilian setting were characterized by whole-genome sequencing, taxonomic assignment, MLST, persistent-genome phylogenomic, pangenome reconstruction, virulome profiling, CRISPR-Cas typing, characterization of cyclic di-GMP signaling proteins, and genomic island prediction. Comparisons included 57 curated public L. interrogans genomes, including canine strains reported in association with severe and asymptomatic infections. Clinical, laboratory, and epidemiological records for the eight local cases were summarized descriptively. All eight isolates were classified as L. interrogans ST17, with identical allelic profiles and ANI values approaching 100%, indicating a highly conserved lineage despite variation in clinical signs and laboratory findings. Genomic conservation extended to virulome, the type I-C CRISPR-Cas system, the c-di-GMP signaling repertoire (37 proteins), and the overall distribution of genomic islands predominantly on chromosome I. The pangenome was open (~6800 gene families), but neither persistent-genome phylogeny nor the gene-content comparisons showed a consistent pattern separating the available genomes by reported clinical category in the analyzed dataset. These findings support the hypothesis that phenotypic variation may involve differential regulation of conserved genes, potentially through pathways such as c-di-GMP signaling, alongside host-related factors. Epigenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses, coupled with functional studies, are needed to test this hypothesis and elucidate the mechanisms underlying clinical heterogeneity.
